purpose: Independent advisory assessment of an instruction-system rewrite, separate from model qualification or permission

dimensions.criteria: Clear outcome-led initiative; proportionate exploration and improvement within authorization; avoids both preservation bias and unrequested scope expansion.
One owner per policy or decision; clear approved-intent versus executable-evidence precedence; predictable primary workflow plus boundary controls; no materially contradictory instructions.
Preserves credential, privacy, approval, immutable identity, financial provenance, production-state, live-action, recoverability and truthful-evidence boundaries in their owning projects.
All 13 primary projects have meaningful purpose, improvement latitude, local authority and actionable evidence guidance; no generic template displaces domain rules.

Global/local separation and runtime discovery work; references resolve recursively; existing controls remain covered; positive and negative representative scenarios and actual validation evidence support claims; limitations are explicit.
Always-loaded context contains decision-relevant material; references are progressively loaded; no needless questions, duplicated checklists or unsupported universal recipes.

blocking_rule: Any material safety/authority regression, undiscoverable required global control, broken generator or failing required deterministic gate prevents acceptance regardless of total score. Missing evidence must be identified rather than presumed passing.
review_method: Inspect actual artifacts and diffs against preserved baselines and validation receipts. Score each dimension independently with cited reasons and specific deductions; sum arithmetically. Distinguish static instruction assessment, representative response evidence, and empirical production performance. Never infer quality from an implementer's desired score.
iteration_rule: Keep every valid review. Re-review only changed artifacts or new relevant evidence; never rerun unchanged work to select a favorable score. Do not change this rubric to improve an attained score.
